subject: Clarify processor roles, SCCs and third-party hosting for Acuity order form
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acumed.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: DPA & SCCs — subprocessor list and hosting locations

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and our legal team are reviewing the order form + MSA and flagged a couple of open items on data protection before we can proceed to signature:

- We need a current subprocessor list and a commitment on where customer data may be hosted (US/EU).
- We require incorporation of the EU SCCs (or equivalent) and clarity on how Redwood proposes to flow those down to subprocessors.
- Our privacy team requests a short Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) describing safeguards for cross-border flows.
- Please attach SOC 2 evidence and any recent penetration test summaries.

Can you route this to your legal/privacy folks and share a proposed redline for the DPA and the hosting commitments? Procurement would like keep moving — target signing by next week if possible.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
General Counsel, AcuMed Health

--

Quick ask from our side: does AcuMed need subprocessors named in the order form, or is a maintained published list (weekly snapshot) acceptable? Procurement preference noted in your note; want to surface that to legal.

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T14:22:00-04:00
Subject: Proposed DPA redlines and SCC incorporation method

Sara — attaching a short redline set to the standard Redwood DPA. High-level notes below:

1) SCCs: we propose incorporation by reference via an exhibit that lists the current SCC text and a mechanism to adopt updated SCCs (mutual written agreement or standard adoption clause).

2) Subprocessors: we can offer a maintained published subprocessor list (weekly snapshot) plus a clause requiring notice and an objection window for critical subprocessors for sensitive data processing. For procurement needs we can also add a column for hosting region (US/EU) per subprocessor.

3) Limited subcontracting: we are not able to accept an absolute ban on subcontracting. Proposed compromise: Redwood may engage subprocessors but will provide notice and a 30-day cure/objection period; we can commit to reasonable efforts to avoid moving EU customer data outside the EU without prior written agreement.

4) Transfer Impact Addendum: see Neha's suggested TIA below; I propose we include a short TIA exhibit summarizing safeguards (encryption in transit/at rest, contractual controls, SCCs, on-demand audit evidence).

Please review the attached redline (tracked changes) and return any material counterpoints. I also flagged a clause where procurement asked for export-controls annotations on the order form — want to ensure the commercial team is aligned before docuSign.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: redlines_from_laura_20260830.docx

On Thu, Aug 30, 2026 at 10:03 AM jasmine_liu@redwood.ai wrote:
> Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (legal) and Neha (privacy) to propose redlines and the TIA summary...
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T16:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA redlines and SCC incorporation method

Laura / Jasmine — added a short TIA summary and evidence schedule. Key points:

- TIA: we'll include a 1-page TIA exhibit that documents the categories of transfers (processor->subprocessor, cross-border support access), legal basis (SCCs), and compensating measures (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, strict access controls, KMS for keys).
- Subprocessor evidence: propose a cadence — published list + SOC 2 summary for any new subprocessor onboarding; offer to provide SOC 2 report under NDA for critical subprocessors.
- Hosting commitment: we can commit to region controls for customer-designated EU-data customers where the order form selects EU residency, with an exception path for disaster recovery (DR) and transient failover (we will notify customers in such events).

Attachments: short TIA summary and an internal checklist for evidence delivery. I recommend we accept the notice + 30-day objection window approach for subprocessors and push back on a hard prohibition — that would block necessary operational flexibility.

Neha Kapoor
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acumed.com>

Cc: procurement@acumed.com
Date: 2026-08-31T11:18:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA redlines and SCC incorporation method

Thanks Laura / Neha — overall this is helpful. A couple of items from our side:

- Procurement insists on explicit listing of primary hosting locations in the order form (US / EU) for the pilot. A published list is helpful but they want the order form annotated for the initial rollouts.
- We remain uncomfortable with unilateral subcontracting rights even with notice — can Redwood accept a limited carve (no subcontracting for storage of EU personal data outside EU without prior written consent)?
- Liability and indemnity: we marked higher liability caps in our counter-redline document (attached). Please review and advise on flexibility.

We attached a single PDF with our redlines and a procurement note. Let us know if legal leadership (or commercial) needs to weigh in — procurement will pause signature if we don’t resolve these by EOD Friday.

Sara

--
Attachment stubs: acuity_redlines_20260831.pdf
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acumed.com>, procurement@acumed.com
Date: 2026-09-01T20:11:00-04:00
Subject: Next steps — decision for limited carve + exec sign-off path

Team — summary and proposed path:

1) Hosting annotation: we will add an Order Form field that captures the primary hosting region for the pilot (US or EU) and include an explicit column in the subprocessor snapshot for hosting location. That should satisfy Procurement's ask for the initial rollout.

2) Subcontracting carve: recommend we offer the limited carve AcuMed requests: "Redwood will not subcontract storage of EU personal data outside the EU without Customer's prior written consent, except for transient DR/failover as defined in the TIA exhibit." This preserves operationalability while addressing AcuMed's core concern.

3) Liability redlines: Laura — please prepare a short note on flexibility and escalation path (commercial approval thresholds). If legal can propose net-new language, we'll surface to Aditya / Rishi for commercial sign-off.

4) Evidence delivery: Neha to commit to SOC 2 under NDA for any critical subprocessors and a cadence for published updates.

5) Timeline & escalation: Procurement wants resolution by EOD Friday (2026-09-03). If legal leadership sign-off is needed we should escalate today — Laura: do you need your manager looped?

Action items: Laura (redline response / liability note), Neha (TIA exhibit final), Aditya/Rishi (commercial redlines on caps). I will notify Sara and send an amended Order Form + DPA once we have Laura's language.

-Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
